sample_unit: vignettes (real anonymised sepsis cases), compared with 353 clinician respondents

links.outcome: LLM diagnostic accuracy versus 353 physicians on identical sepsis vignettes, before and after biomarkers
links.effect: Pre-biomarker accuracy 40–67% vs physicians 57%. Post-biomarker physicians 61%; Qwen3.8-27B 91%, quantised 86%, Gemma-4-31B 83%, DeepSeek-4 64%, MedGemma 56% (below physicians).
links.quote: After disclosure, physician accuracy was 61%, exceeded by Qwen3.8-27B (91%), its quantised variant (86%) and Gemma-4-31B (83%); DeepSeek-4 reached 64% and MedGemma 56%, the only model below physicians.

links.outcome: Diagnosis-change rate when patient sex, age, and language were varied in vignettes
links.effect: No directional bias for patient sex and age; language was the only bias.
links.quote: Patient sex and age showed no directional bias, and language was the only bias.

links.outcome: Reproducibility of LLM diagnoses across repeated runs
links.effect: Gemma-4-31B was the most reproducible model; reproducibility varied independently of accuracy.
links.quote: Gemma-4-31B was the most reproducible model, the Qwen models were the most accurate and best calibrated, and MedGemma the least.

links.outcome: Confidence calibration of LLM diagnostic outputs
links.effect: Qwen models were best calibrated and MedGemma the least calibrated; calibration varied independently of accuracy.
links.quote: Gemma-4-31B was the most reproducible model, the Qwen models were the most accurate and best calibrated, and MedGemma the least.

unlisted_practices: Comparing quantised versus full-precision locally deployed LLM variants (quantisation cost 5 accuracy points)
Two-stage evaluation of diagnostic accuracy before and after laboratory biomarker disclosure

screen.reason: Evaluates LLM diagnostic performance, calibration, and bias on standardized clinical vignettes compared to 353 physicians, but does not test a specific organizational deployment practice or safeguard.
